title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: RegenAll + PCA&D: (Mini) Enviro-Zine Making 101: Grades 7 - 10
location: Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration, 204 North Prince Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
In 2026, RegenAll’s Youth Climate Art Exhibition will be a pre-event component of RegenAll’s Annual Climate Summit. Students from around the county will have the opportunity to express their vision of a thriving, resilient, and sustainable “green future” to promote creative and hopeful thinking for the next generation. We hope that their work will inspire decision-makers, lawmakers, and community members to see a better future for our shared environment. The exhibition will be held November 8 – 15 at Pennsylvania College of Art & Design’s Welcome Center (241 N. Prince Street, Lancaster, PA ) with an opening reception on Friday, November 13, 2026 from 5 – 7:30 pm.  



One way for young community members to submit work is in one of our free workshops held at PCA&D! Join us! This is a mini-zine making class for students in grades 7-10. This class will cover how to make an 8-page mini-zine and its many uses. The main goal of this class is to understand what goes into making a mini-zine and how they can be used as a tool for communicating ideas and opinions through art. In addition to mini-zine production, students will learn mixed-media techniques; they will first brainstorm ideas for their zines and create a hard copy by collaging from recycled magazines and hand-drawn illustrations. Then, once they are done with their hard copy, they will learn how to copy and fold their zines. Walking away with 6 mini zines with their idea of a more environmentally conscious future. Instructor: Laurence Jacoby Saturday, October 17 10 AM – 12 PM

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Challenging Ride (A) - Sunday Worlds (32R)
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Anticipated average pace: **18-20 mph**

Cue and GPX link: [https://ridewithgps.com/routes/45180282](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/45180282)

This ride has been a classic in Lancaster County for a long time. The route is unique in that it starts and finishes at two different locations. As a result, most cyclists ride to the start and then ride home from the finish.

It starts at the Millersville Mart: 473 N George St, Millersville, PA 17551 (pictured) and the finish is at the new Bierhall Brewing Company: 1703 New Holland Pike, Lancaster, PA 17601. The Bierhall is open for lunch, so riders are welcome to stop in after the ride.

**This is a Challenging (A) level ride and intended to be a NO DROP RIDE.** The ride leader will ride at the advertised average speed and will do his/her best to keep the group together with regroupings and a sweeper may also be appointed at the start. **Please do not join this ride if you are not willing to stick with the group.** If maintaining an 18-20mph average is beyond your current ability level, please consider joining an "Advanced" ride first.

Helmets are mandatory. No earbuds. Please bring water and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).

To eliminate passing around a pen and paper waiver, we require an LBC Club membership and Meetup RSVP below to join this ride.

Being on Meetup does not mean you are a club member. [Join here](https://www.lancasterbikeclub.net/content.aspx?page_id=60&club_id=257148).

Your RSVP is your agreement to abide by the club's [Code of Conduct](https://lancbikeclub.clubexpress.com/content.aspx?page_id=22&club_id=257148&module_id=323984),

[Rules of the Road](https://lancbikeclub.clubexpress.com/content.aspx?page_id=22&club_id=257148&module_id=325159), and [Ride Waiver](https://lancasterbikeclub.net/docs.ashx?id=454318)

title: Figure Drawing: Extended Pose Workshop with Evan Kitson at PCA&D
location: Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration, 204 North Prince Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
In this single session long-pose figure drawing workshop, artist, anatomist, and instructor Evan Kitson will guide you through the main stages of building a single drawing from the blank page to a resolved artwork.  



Through lecture, demonstration, and personalized feedback at the drawing easel, you’ll learn how to navigate the timeless challenges of gesture, proportion, structure, mark-making and material use, while also studying the nude human figure through artistic anatomy and perception concepts. You’ll leave this workshop with a worked and well-observed figure drawing, and the many ideas and concepts surrounding its construction that you can then bring into your personal work at home. Evan will be teaching and demonstrating using graphite materials, but you’re welcome to use any erasable drawing medium you prefer. This workshop has been designed for the “intermediate level” artist, but there’s a lot here for both the beginner and the more advanced artist as well. If you’re interested in figure drawing and everything that comes with the challenge of working from the live model, this is the perfect workshop for you!

title: Children's Chapel
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

description:
Join us for WORK FLOW, a showcase highlighting some of the most active and compelling voices in the 717 independent music scene. Part performance and part process breakdown, the night offers a look into how local artists build their music from the ground up. 



Featured Artists: 




benOAKS – Independent hip-hop artist, producer, and graphic designer. His single “Empathy” (with 66notes) is in national indie and college radio rotation, with his next single “Fall Down” (ft. Karma Star) dropping October 23 ahead of his upcoming EP.

the BJEWELLED – Rounding out the featured showcase with their distinct sound and creative approach.

description:

via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.

title: Red Rose Blue Star Mom's Chapter Meeting
SparkDate: Loxley's Fall Social
location: Loxley’s Restaurant, 500 Centerville Rd, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17601, United States
description:
A whimsical treehouse bar unlike anything else in Central Pennsylvania, and it’s at its coziest once fall sets in. With Robin Hood-inspired woodwork, a tree growing right through the center, and a heated outdoor bar for crisp October nights, the space is full of charm and character. Add good food and a laid-back atmosphere, and you’ve got the perfect fall night out for singles who want real conversations with real people, not another swipe.  



How the night works: You check in with a host and get a name tag — there’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements: 



First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play — that’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people.  



Then the structure drops away and it’s open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it’s working. By that point you’ve already met most of the room, so nobody is starting cold — which is the part a bar full of strangers never gets right. 



 Last: one-on-ones with the people you haven’t already sat with. Near the end you privately note anyone you’d like to see again; it takes under a minute and nobody else sees it. If someone noted you back, that’s a match, and you both get it that night rather than after some review period.  



Why it’s built this way:Everyone in the room came out on purpose on a Tuesday night. That’s a filter no dating app has. The structure does the hard part — you never have to work out how to start or end a conversation — and the other awkward part, finding out whether it was mutual, is handled quietly for you afterwards. 21+ with valid ID Tickets and full details: https://sparkdate.date/l/lx2-figlancaster

On Tuesday, October 13, we will start a 5-week Fall Contemplative Citizenship series in which we will reflect on various lines from the prayer, exploring what it means to embody this prayer in both our personal lives and in our civic responsibilities, especially during this election season when our country feels divided and stressed.

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

Join local GM Matt as he runs a variety of Tabletop Role Playing Games that rotate each month. No experience in any system is required and anyone interested in dipping their toes into the TTRPG world are welcomed and encouraged to join in on the fun!This month's game is: DaggerheartThe town of Cadence is one steeped in superstition. It was built over a century ago when a large copper mine was established nearby promising wealth and prosperity. However, the mine was located within the soft grounds of a swamp leading to poor living conditions for the miners on shift, frequent cave-ins, hazardous gasses, and a variety of other fatal accidents. Disregarding the cries from the public to shut the mine down the owner of the copper mine, Liviett Truce kept her operation going for nearly 30 years with little care of her employed miners.One day rumors of a creature stalking the mining camps in the swamp made their way back to Cadence. Miners would go missing, claw marks raked through the canvas of their tents, trails of blood leading out into the murky waters of the swamp. The town erupted in a panic and the workers left the camps on strike. Liviett wanted to put an end to the strike swiftly and as frugally as possible so she decided to go visit the now emptied mining camps to prove no such creature exists. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Screening of the documentary Welcome To Yiddishland
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Movie & Film, Adults, Seniors

Welcome to Yiddishland offers an upbeat, witty and timely exploration of this international community of artists, who are rediscovering and revitalising Yiddish culture. Whilst being a highly entertaining Arts film, full of joyous music, and performances; it also reframes our understanding of Jewish culture and identity.The film is timely in that it breaks down the current reductionist stereotyping of Jews that allow anti-Semitic hate to fester and constructive discourse to suffocate. It probes the nuanced aspects of Jewish culture and identity to reveal the multi-layered aspects of what it means to identify as Jewish and engage in Jewish culture.Through intimate interviews and rare behind-the-scenes access to some of the world's top musicians and performers working in Yiddish, we showcase the innovative works of artists who use this ancient language as a vehicle for addressing contemporary issues such as Queer identity, the refugee crisis, war and authoritarianism.This community is not large in overall numbers but they are global, spreading from Mexico and Buenos Aires, Berlin, New York, Paris, Melbourne and more.They are having a big impact. Indeed they are driving a renaissance in Yiddish Arts and Culture.Film runs 1 hour and 35 minutes.

title: Mercy Seminar, Term 3
location: Zoom Video Conferencing, PA, United States
description:
With Father David Peck
and Professor Randall Zachman
Entirely on Zoom 
Now in its seventh year, the 2026 Mercy Seminar invites you to explore the profound insights that different faith traditions offer about embracing life and navigating death with grace. How can the certainty of death inspire us to cultivate a deeper focus and a heart full of gratitude, transforming potential feelings of anxiety into a courageous appreciation for the present moment? Is death merely “nothing at all,” or does it open the gateway to an eternal adventure beyond this life? 
Join us as we delve into selected sacred readings from Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, and Muslim scriptures, along with enlightening contemporary secular spiritual writings. Together, we will uncover the wisdom that encourages us to live our best lives and face death not with fear, but with hope and understanding. 
In term three (September 24 – October 29), we will focus on Christian understandings of resurrection and eternal life, beginning with the hope of future resurrection life in Paul’s letters and the expectation of eternal life now in the Gospel of John. We will follow the development of these themes in Christian and Spiritualist traditions, including Emanuel Swedenborg’s provocative visions of the soul’s journey after death. 
Classes meet on six consecutive Thursday evenings via Zoom from 7:00 to 8:30 PM EST. Each term stands alone, but when taken together, offers a layered understanding as our knowledge of the issues increases. All sessions are recorded and available to participants for asynchronous viewing. 

Each session will be recorded in Zoom and available for viewing for those who have completed their registration. 
Cost: $75/term, includes access to course readings, recorded sessions for
asynchronous viewing, instructor office hours and podcasts. 
Scholarships are available; please email Kate Umble Smucker for more information.

title: Make & Take: Glass Christmas Tree
location: Bird-in-Hand Artisan Village, 2705 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA, 17505, United States
description:
Learn to create a custom piece of seasonal decor 
Just in time for the holidays, you can learn how to transform ordinary materials into treasured artwork. In this 90-minute workshop, local artisan Karen Worst will guide you through the process of selecting the glass, beads and wooden pieces you’ll use to make a still-life picture of a Christmas tree, putting the pieces together with resin binder and, finally, matting and framing your creation to take home. Choose from a variety of colors to match your décor. 
Before retiring, Karen Worst worked as a nurse by day and created art in her downtime. Today, she makes one-of-a-kind, nature-inspired art with glass, recycled glass, resin, acrylic paint and other simple materials. 
Reserve your space today! 
$30 per person includes instruction and all material for framed 6-x-6-inch finished art.

————————————————–
Presented by Drums Etc
————————————————–
The Pennsylvania Drum Show is BACK for the Fall of 2026! This Marketplace, Showcase and Community event draws drum enthusiasts from across America to celebrate everything drums & percussion! Started in 1995, this is the 2nd longest running drum show in the country! Lancaster drum retailer, Drums Etc. took the reins from Jack Lawton (Founder) back in 2023 and every year elevates the experience! This all-day event (12-7:30) takes place on the Rock Lititz Campus inside the premier music venue: Mickey’s Black Box. The  public is encouraged to pop-in or stay all day! 
Attendees will enjoy a massive indoor vendor Marketplace filled with New, Used & Vintage drum gear, try the latest gear from drum/cymbal manufactures in the “Industry Alley” section, watch Educational Clinics by Gregg Bissonette [Ringo Starr All Star Band], Rob Mitzner [Author/Educator] & Fr. Hyacinth Cordell [Priest/Acclaimed Drummer], participate in Interactive Presentations (“Becoming a Durable Drummer” [Drummer Rx], Zildjian “Cymbal Talk”, Drums Etc. Student Showcase, Drum Circle [The Love Drums]), have the opportunity to sell gear in the Consignment Marketplace (Item tags $5, $20/set), and get to meet their heroes in the Meet & Greet Lounge (Tony Royster Jr [Katy Perry, Jay-Z], Matt Greiner [August Burns Red], Jason Bittner [Shadows Fall] +more!). Every attendee receives a Raffle ticket with entry for a chance to win prizes donated by Drums Etc and industry supporters. Bar and concessions are available all day inside the MBB venue, in addition to, food vendors out front and on the Rock Lititz Campus. 
In a conscious effort to give back to the local music scene, Drums Etc. partnered with local businesses to elevate the 2026 show. A&E Audiology & Hearing Aid Center is co-sponsor for the event. Additionally, presentations & clinics will take place on the “Keller Pro Audio Stage”, attendees will buy/sell gear in the “Reason & Fritz Entertainment Consignment Market” and meet their heroes in the “SRCC Meet & Greet Lounge” (Susquehanna River Creative Conspiracy). 
There are two ticketing options for the event. General Admission gains access to all clinics, presentations and features throughout the day from 1-7:30pm. During this time, attendees will have full access to the event marketplace, in addition to the meet & greet lounge. VIP Early Access gains access 1 hour early to the event space (Noon-1). This is recommended for collectors looking for rare vintage pieces or attendees that wish to avoid large crowds. Kids under 10 years old are FREE! 
Visit the official show page here for full details & to register for booths! 
For more information about the show, booking information and a comprehensive list of VIP Artists attending the show visit Drums Etc. 
CONTACT: 717-394-3786 or Adam@DrumsEtc.com

title: The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

🌿 BEAUTY OR BANE? THE SECRET LIFE OF YOUR GARDEN 💀Vibrant lavender and mauve blossoms sway in the breeze while butterflies dip and dance above. With every rustle of foliage, delicate white buds flash in the sunlight. It’s the ultimate dream landscape—an idyllic, peaceful sanctuary designed for pure relaxation.But look closer. Hidden within this botanical paradise, unexpected danger might be lurking right in plain sight.Is that vivid red berry harmless or a hazard?What secret is that unusual violet flower stalk hiding?Could your pet's favorite sunbathing spot be surrounded by toxic greenery?Uncover the truth behind the beauty! Join speakers Cynthia Trussell, Indigo Bowser, and Kathy Vu of the Penn State Master Gardeners for The Treachery of Botany: Poisonous Garden Plants. In this eye-opening 45-minute presentation (followed by a Q&A session), you'll learn how to identify ordinary, uncommon, cultivated, and wild poisonous plants in your landscape-- discover what makes them tick, and master easy, practical ways to manage them safely.Keep your loved ones safe while keeping your sanctuary gorgeous. Don't miss it-- turn your garden into a true, worry-free paradise!

This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. A Spooktacular Night Under the Stars!
Celebrate the spooky season with an evening of celestial wonders! Join North Museum at Millport Conservancy on Thursday, October 29, from 7:00–9:00 PM for a FREE night of stargazing! 
Explore the night sky as we turn our telescopes toward dazzling stars, the magnificent rings of Saturn, and even Algol, the mysterious “Demon Star,” as it begins to dim during its celestial eclipse. If we’re lucky, we might even catch a shooting star or two from the tail end of the Orionid meteor shower! 
Costumes are encouraged, so dress up, bring a lawn chair, and settle in for a hauntingly good night of astronomy and discovery! 
When: Thursday, October 29 | 7:00–9:00 PM
Where: Millport Conservancy
Admission: FREE and open to the public! 
This event is weather permitting. In the event of unfavorable conditions, cancellation will be announced by 2:00 PM on October 29.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

title: American Disasters
location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:
Discussion, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Best for adults and older interested teens. Registration is appreciated but not required if space allows.American Disasters is a six-session PowerPoint series. Dr. Robert Frick, historian and presenter, will share the stories and facts related to six events that significantly impacted the United States. The stories of the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the Johnstown Flood of 1889, the San Francisco Earthquake of 1906, Hurricane Agnes in the Susquehanna Basin in 1972, the Asian Flu Pandemic of 1957-58, and the Sinking of the USS Indianapolis will be shared during this program. Participants should prepare for lively presentations filled with interesting facts and peppered with humor. Dr. Frick’s goal is education with a smile.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - “In Search of 10,000, and 10,000, and 10,000 Birds”
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Peter Kaestner, legendary birder and retired diplomat 
Peter Kaestner relates his life-long quest to see 10,000 species of birds – a quest that was almost derailed on February, 2024, when another birder claimed the record just hours before Peter saw is last bird in the Philippines.  Since then, Peter has maintained his quest, ultimately observing 10,000 species in the eBird and AviList taxonomies. 
Peter is a retired U.S. diplomat and an active independent birder who has spent a lifetime sharing his passion. On February 9, 2024, he achieved his ultimate goal when he saw his 10,000th species of bird, an Orange-tufted Spiderhunter in Mindanao, the Philippines on the IOC taxonomy. On October 21, 2025, he reached 10,000 on eBird, and on November 11, 2025, he recorded his 10,000th species on the new AviList harmonized world bird list. Always a birder, Peter took his first international trip at age ten, when he visited the Bahamas with his brother and mentor Hank. As of December 2025, he has birded in 196 eBird countries and territories. He is recognized by the Guinness Book of Records for having the world’s biggest life lists eBird (10022) and AviList (10,008) and as the first person to see a representative of every bird family – a feat that he accomplished in October, 1986. The highlight of Peter’s birding career came in 1989. Just 50 kilometers east of the Colombian capital, he discovered a bird new to science, the Cundinamarca Antpitta (Grallaria kaestneri). Peter graduated from Friends School Baltimore, where he received the William S. Pike science award and all-state honors in lacrosse. He studied Biology at Cornell University, graduating in 1976. Peter served in the Peace Corps in Zaire (Democratic Republic of Congo) as a secondary-school science teacher in 1976-1978 and joined the U.S. Department of State in June, 1980. During his 36-year career as a U.S. diplomat, he helped negotiate the UN Desertification Convention and a protocol amending the 1916 Migratory Bird Convention with Canada. He represented the United States at Conferences of the Parties of the Ramsar Convention and CITES. Peter has lived in 12 different countries: India, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, USA, Colombia, Malaysia, Namibia, Guatemala, Brazil, Egypt, Afghanistan, and Germany. Peter retired in 2016 from the State Department at the rank of Minister-Counselor. Peter loves sharing his passion for birds by writing articles, leading bird walks and tours, supporting local conservation efforts, and giving illustrated lectures on birds around the world. After the Colombian Government made peace with the FARC guerilla group, Peter helped it bring economic development to rural areas by promoting bird tourism. He also worked with the American Bird Conservancy and a Colombian NGO (Fundación Camaná) to preserve critical habitat of the Cundinamarca Antpitta in the east Andes. In 2019, Peter became a part-time tour leader for Rockjumper Birding Tours, in 2021 he became a VIP for Swarovski Optik, in 2023 he was appointed ambassador of the American Bird Conservancy, and in 2024 he received the American Birding Association’s Roger Tory Peterson Lifetime Achievement Award. Peter is married to Kimberly Vreeland Kaestner, and has two grown daughters, Laurel and Katie.

Each guest will go home with a Sourdough Starter Kit that includes everything they need to start baking immediately: 

1 jar of active, hydrated, ready-to use sourdough starter
A professional-grade class fermentation jar that they can use to hold and maintain their starter
A traditional wooden spurtle to stir deep into the jar for a perfect mix with less mess
A stylish breathable cotton bonnet for the jar
Professional instruction sheets, including step-by-step feeding guides and schedule, a beginner-friendly recipe, and trouble-shooting tips

Sourdough has prebiotics, or healthy gut bacteria. It also has less gluten and a lower glycemic index than some other breads.

There’s no business meeting and no required agenda. We can talk about whatever interests us: our lives, ideas, books, politics, culture, what’s happening in Lancaster, what we’ve been thinking about lately — or anything else that comes up around the table.
We’ll also talk a little about whether we’d like to make this a regular gathering and, if so, what **we** would like it to be.
For our first get-together, we’re meeting at Loxley’s — an especially fun place to begin, with its Robin Hood and Sherwood Forest theme.
And since every good Sherwood Forest gathering needs her:
**Maid Marian is welcome at our table.**

Step back in time with living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the harrowing story of Clotz's Battalion-- part of the legendary "Flying Camp" mobile reserve.Relive the tension of November 1776 at the Battle of Fort Lee, discover the courageous stories of local soldiers fighting for a brand-new nation, and see how modern historians uncover the past to keep their legacy alive. Don't miss this immersive journey into the fight for independence!Registration is encouraged!A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Presenter Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

title: Klezmer and Jewish Music by members of Quartet Harriet: Christopher Brooks, violin and Laurie Reese, violoncello
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Music, Everyone

Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music. Based in Lancaster, PA, Laurie has freelanced and concertized extensively throughout the United States and Europe.This performance is made possible through a grant from the Yiddish Book Center. Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. location: Lancaster, LPL Community Room
description:

Winnie-the-Pooh is celebrating its 100th birthday this year! The stories A.A. Milne created have become classics that are as beloved now as they were when they were first published in October 1926. In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart 😉

title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group
description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County
Life can be frustrating and distressing!
Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

Donations to the Being One Center are greatly appreciated

title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies"
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Club President Andy McGann 
Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

title: Coffee & Crossing: Washington's Winter of 1776
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War!Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group

Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Swoon Squad: A Romance TBR Book Club
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center A
description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! #### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Girl Scout Badge Workshops- Mechanical Engineering
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Badge Workshops for Daisies through Juniors
The Lancaster Science Factory is pleased to offer an expanded menu of Girl Scout workshops designed to educate, challenge, and empower scouts while completing badge requirements. 
Workshops are 1 hour unless otherwise noted. Register a single scout or the whole troop for upcoming workshops listed below. 
  
Mechanical Engineering Badge Workshops
Our hands-on Mechanical Engineering badge workshops cover the following badges: 

Daisies Mechanical Engineering Badge 1: Board Game Design
Brownies Mechanical Engineering Badge 3: Race Car Design
Juniors Mechanical Engineering Badge 2: Balloon Car Design

Mechanical Engineering workshops will be offered on the following dates: 
Saturday, November 14, 2026
–Daisies from 12:30-1:30 pm (register here) 
–Brownies from 2-3 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3:30-4:30 pm (register here) 
Saturday, January 16, 2027
–Daisies from 12:30-1:30 pm (register here) 
–Brownies from 2-3 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3:30-4:30 pm (register here) 
Saturday, February 27, 2027
–Daisies from 12:30-1:30 pm (register here) 
–Brownies from 2-3 pm (register here) 
–Juniors from 3:30-4:30 pm (register here) 
  
Can’t make it to a scheduled workshop? Reach out to Megan Stoltzfus at mstoltzfus@tlsf.org to schedule a private workshop. Availability is limited for private workshops, so we recommend scheduling ahead by a minimum of 1-2 months if possible.
Program attendance, cancellation, and refund policy.

Cancellations (by the registrant) received less than one week prior to the workshop will be subject to a refund of 1/2 of the total registration cost for that workshop. Cancellations received prior to that shall receive a full refund.
Workshops canceled by the Lancaster Science Factory for ANY reason will be refunded fully.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)
source: Meetup: The Creative House of Lancaster

title: Girl Scout Badge Workshops (Robotics)
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Badge Workshops for Daisies through Juniors
The Lancaster Science Factory is pleased to offer an expanded menu of Girl Scout workshops designed to educate, challenge, and empower scouts while completing badge requirements. 
Workshops are 1 hour unless otherwise noted. Register a single scout or the whole troop for upcoming workshops listed below. 
  
Robotics Badge Workshops
Learn all about robotics with our hands-on Robotics Badge workshops! All workshops cover the Robotics Badge 1 for each troop level. 
Robotics workshops will be offered on the following dates: 
Saturday, October 17, 2026
–Daisies and Brownies from 1:30-2:30 pm (register here)

Program attendance, cancellation, and refund policy.

Cancellations (by the registrant) received less than one week prior to the workshop will be subject to a refund of 1/2 of the total registration cost for that workshop. Cancellations received prior to that shall receive a full refund.
Workshops canceled by the Lancaster Science Factory for ANY reason will be refunded fully.

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in
